newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise again at midday as bonds rally.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise again at midday as bonds rally.

text.p: Stocks rallied yet again Wednesday, driven by fresh optimism over interest rates and inflation and the growing belief that the budget deal and tax cuts announced this week will provide a long-term boost to financial markets.
Just after 1 p.m., the Dow Jones industrial average was up 65.73 points at 8,240.26, as the index pushed further into record territory.

Stocks benefited from falling long-term interest rates. In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury jumped 7/8 of a point, or $8.75 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.32 percent, the lowest level in 16 months, from 6.39 percent Tuesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

"Bonds are having a very good day and that helps stocks," said Barbara Marcin, vice president of Citibank Global Asset Management. "All recent information indicates we have low inflation and moderate growth. The balanced budget deal and the proposed capital gains tax cut are also driving stocks."
"Both bonds and stocks have been working in absolute concert in a perfect market," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp.
A heady combination of benign inflation, moderate economic growth and the balanced budget agreement have propelled financial markets higher, analysts said.
Stocks and bonds also got a boost as investors digested details of the deal between President Clinton and Reblicans to balance the budget and cut capital gains taxes.

The market's strength was broad-based, with financial, drug and technology issues all gaining. Advancing issues swamped declines by a 19-8 margin on the New York Stock Exchange, where volume was active at 330 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index, laden with high-technology stocks, rose 12.24 points to 1,584.56.
New home sales data for June and May confirmed the general thinking about the economy and gave an early lift to stocks, market watchers said.
The Commerce Department said June new home sales rose 6.1 percent to a 819,000 unit annual rate. But the government revised the May figures down sharply.
"Housing starts were revised to a ridiculous degree in May," Stein said. "Combined, they both showed moderation."

The gains in the bond market dropped the 30-year bond yield to its lowest level since March 1996. As rates fall, investors typically look to higher-yielding investments such as stocks for better returns.
Some analysts cautioned that the market still faces the monthly jobs report for July, due Friday.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks added 8.49 points to 950.78.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.63 points to 643.83.
